page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing users to attach external high-performance storage volumes.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance and memory write bandwidth fall into the average range. However, memory read-only bandwidth for large blocks is weak, landing in the bottom 25 percent, which suggests a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive workloads accessing large datasets. In contrast, text processing and text generation for small language models show strong performance, while prompt processing for medium-sized models is weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8as_v6 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. Given its strong single-core processing capabilities and balanced memory allocation, this server is well-suited for web serving, text processing, software compilation, and running lightweight database or application servers that do not require massive local storage or high-bandwidth memory access.
